items.headline: Warranty-claim short-payment audit for HVAC/refrigeration shops
items.detail: A model reads the fields out of the manufacturer's remittance and the filed claim; our own arithmetic re-derives the manufacturer's published payment schedule (allowed hours per repair code, multiple-repair increment, travel rule, per-claim caps) against what was actually paid, per line, with the schedule version and page cited. Sells the finding and a resubmission packet, never the human chase.
items.impact: Recon 2026-10-26, score 79 of 100. $1.50/call metered (LLM class band $0.50-3.00) against a modelled cost of about $0.22, so it clears the 3x margin rule. Weakest link named in the PRD: no owned audience for trade contractors. CanopyProof (approved 2026-10-18) is still unstarted, so this is a queue-ordering decision, not just a go/no-go.

items.headline: The factory could not deploy for 20 hours — the new copy gate scanned a folder a clean build does not have; fixed
items.detail: Measured 2026-10-23 15:30Z: Coolify deployments 2544 (2026-10-22 19:06:57Z, commit 533e309) and 2553 (19:16:56Z, commit 5a96e75) both FAILED, and the live container still carries SOURCE_COMMIT 7d60f7e from the 16:37 build, so the FacturGate badge-copy fix in 533e309 never went live. Cause: the new prebuild step copy:check ran vibe-lint.mjs against src AND content/launch_videos; that directory is gitignored runtime output, so in a git clone it does not exist and the linter died with ENOENT scandir '/app/content/launch_videos', exit 1, build failed. Reproduced outside Coolify (git clone . /tmp/cleanclone && npm run copy:check -> same ENOENT), so it was not a platform flake and would have blocked every future product push. Fix applied this sweep in package.json only: copy:check runs the src scan exactly as before, then scans content/launch_videos only when the directory exists, printing an explicit 'not present (gitignored runtime output)' line when it does not. Vendored scripts/vibe/* are untouched (verify-vendor still ok, 2 files match their recorded hash). Proven to still bite: a banned-word sentence injected into src/products/registry.ts in the clean clone returns verdict FAIL, exit 1; reverted.
items.impact: Deploys work again and the copy gate still blocks bad copy in src. Reader-facing launch copy is scanned only on a machine that holds the (gitignored) artifacts, which is where it is generated. Reversal: restore the single combined invocation and make launch copy present in the build (commit the copy, or generate the artifacts in the image).
items.reply: @Simon restore the strict copy gate  (only once launch copy exists in the build)

items.detail: Done 2026-10-25 (commit f462e6f), on the owner's message "re-point the growth check" — the reply string this row carried since 2026-10-24. scripts/growth-check.mjs no longer has a product default: the scope is parsed from src/products/registry.ts on every run (slug + status, in registry order), so it measures every entry whose status is not `killed` — ledgerlink, facturgate, parcelproof, caseproof, spendproof, ratchetproof — aggregates them into the fleet totals the gates read, and returns a per_product split beside them. A slug on the command line is a drill-down only; a retired or unknown slug now fails with an explicit product_error instead of reading zero, and rows outside the scope are counted in out_of_scope_event_rows (quarterline 228, factory 1,844, billing 326) so nothing is dropped silently. The runbook (.agents/growth_watchdog.md) and the playbook's marker section now state the registry-derived scope, and the Friday job needed no prompt change — it already ran the script with no argument. Gate scripts/verify-build.sh "Verification passed." on the rebased tree: tsc clean, eslint 0 errors, tokens, verticals, recon cadence, vitest 479/479 (35 files), next build ok, Playwright 110/110, visual-qa 30/30 tiles.

items.headline: ParcelProof reads the carrier's own export, and prices a line with no contract rate card
items.detail: Done 2026-10-25 (commit 95c1e61), on the owner's instruction "Yes implement these" — the reply to the two defects raised in his session: the page asked for two CSVs it never explained, and the rate card (which gated every dollar figure) is the one input most shippers cannot export. Headers are now mapped on a normalised form (case, spacing, punctuation, unit suffix) against a synonym table, so a UPS Billing Center / FedEx billing / ShipStation export is read as it comes: Tracking Number -> tracking, Billed Weight (lb) -> billed_weight_lb, Net Amount -> total_usd. Two columns claiming one field is refused, and an unresolvable field fails naming the columns the file DOES have plus the accepted names. With no rate card, observed-bracket pricing uses the charge the carrier itself billed for that same whole-pound weight in the same carrier/service/zone lane on the same invoice — labelled observed-bracket, never verified, never interpolated; a lane whose charges disagree is dropped and an unobserved lane stays unpriced. A contract card still wins, and the default basis is unchanged for existing agent/API calls. The page now says where the files come from (billing-portal CSV, not the PDF), labels every rate by its source, and ships a demo scenario that shows the new pricing.
items.impact: Closed — a visitor with a carrier export and no rate card now gets a dollar figure priced from the carrier's own charges, instead of an all-zero recovery summary.
